transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your busy day. 

Well... I came in because the ladies at my church thought it would be best if I talked to someone. I guess I've been doing some... well, just some slightly odd things lately. Nothing bad, I promise! It's just... at the church dinners, by the potluck table, I'll pick up the serving spoon and then I just... I kind of freeze. I'll just stand there holding the spoon up in the air, not moving at all. Or... or I'll stand there and fold the exact same stack of napkins over and over again, even when folks are waiting on me to move along. 

I really don't mean to hold up the line or be a nuisance to anyone. I just get a little stuck, I suppose. Does that make sense, Doctor? I hope I'm explaining it alright for you.
When you keep folding the same stack of napkins over and over, do you feel like you have to do it to relieve a strong inner urge?

Oh, no, Doctor, it’s nothing like that. I promise I don't have any... any strong urges or anything bad like that. It’s not like I feel anxious or forced to do it. 

I just... my hands just sort of keep going on their own, I suppose. I don't really even realize I'm doing it until one of the ladies gently taps my shoulder. It’s just a silly little habit, really, nothing for anyone to worry about. Am I answering your question alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed a tremor in your hands when they are resting?

Oh, no, Doctor. No, my hands are... they're nice and steady when I'm just sitting. I haven't noticed any shaking or trembling at all. 

I'm very lucky that way, I suppose. I can still hold my teacup without rattling the saucer, thank goodness! I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so I'm not wasting your time. Is there anything else about my hands you need to know?
When you freeze in one position, if someone gently moves your arm, does it tend to stay in the new position for a while?

Oh, goodness, no. If someone comes up and... and gives my arm a little nudge or tries to guide me, I just snap right out of it. My arm doesn't stay stuck up in the air or anything strange like that, I promise! I just put it right back down and apologize for being in the way. 

The ladies are so sweet about it, they just gently pat me and I get right back to moving. I definitely don't want to make it sound worse than it is—it's just a little pause I take, really. I hope I understood your question right? Does that help you, Doctor?
Have people told you that you often stare straight ahead and have trouble looking up or down?

Oh, no, Doctor, no one has ever said anything like that to me. I don't stare off or have any trouble moving my eyes, I promise. 

I can look up at the ceiling or down at my lap just fine. Sometimes I might just get a little lost in thought, you know how it is when you get to be my age, but I'm definitely not just... staring blankly. I always try to look right at the person I'm talking to. I hope that's the right answer? I really don't want you to think I'm ignoring people or being rude. Am I doing okay with these questions?
When you freeze like that, are you still aware of what’s happening around you?

Oh, yes, absolutely. I hear everything going on around me. I'm just... well, taking a little breather, I suppose. I don't black out or lose my senses, I promise! 

I can hear people talking and the television playing and all of that. I just need a tiny minute before I get going again. I wouldn't want you to think my mind is slipping away from me or anything frightening like that. I'm completely awake and listening when it happens. Is that... does that sound like what you were looking for, Doctor? I'm trying my very best to explain it right so I can be helpful to you.
Have you ever heard voices when no one else was there?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, Doctor, I've never had anything like that happen. I know... well, I know sometimes people can get a little confused as they get older, but I certainly don't hear any voices or anything spooky like that. Just my own thoughts, and... and maybe the neighbors through the wall sometimes, but real people! 

I really hope you don't think I'm... well, losing my mind or going crazy. I try very hard to keep sharp and stay on top of things. I haven't heard anyone talking when they aren't there, I promise you that. Is that a good sign? I hope I'm still doing okay with all your questions.
Have people ever told you that your speech is hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Well... maybe just a tiny bit, but it's nothing serious, I promise you. I just get a little chatty, that's all! Sometimes when the ladies ask me about... oh, the blankets we're making, or about choir practice, I really do mean to give them a straight answer. I try my very best to. But I suppose my words just sort of run off a bit. I'll start talking and before I know it, I've gone from talking about string beans to the Sunday hymns, and then right over to how my roses are doing. 

And... well, sometimes folks do look at me like they can't quite find what I'm saying. But it's just because I have so much I want to share with them, you know? Just an older lady rambling a bit. That's perfectly normal, isn't it, Doctor? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I really do try to be a good conversationalist and not confuse anyone. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right answers today.
After one of these times when you freeze or get stuck, do you ever find that you cannot remember what happened during it?

Oh, no, Doctor, not at all! I remember every little thing, I really do. Like I... well, like I mentioned just a little bit ago, I hear the television and the talking, and when I get moving again, I know exactly what went on. I don't lose time or anything scary like that. 

I wouldn't want you to worry that my memory is failing me, or that I'm getting... you know, senile. My mind is still sharp as a tack for my age, I promise you. I remember it all just fine, clear as a bell. I hope that puts your mind at ease? I'm trying to be very careful with my words so I don't give you the wrong impression. Am I still doing alright with your questions?
Have people told you that your face often looks expressionless, even when you’re talking about something emotional?

Oh, heavens no. I try to always keep a nice smile on my face, especially when I'm talking to folks. I wouldn't want anyone to think I'm... well, cold or unfriendly, you know? My friends always say I wear my heart on my sleeve. If I'm happy, you can see it right away, and if I'm a little teary about something, well, I suppose that shows too. 

I think it's just so important to be warm and polite to people, don't you? I really hope I don't look blank or... or like a statue to you right now! I'm trying very hard to be good company and answer everything properly. Do I look alright to you, Doctor? I hope I'm still doing okay.
Have people told you that you sometimes behave in ways that seem very odd or inappropriate for the situation?

Oh, dear... well... I suppose that's actually why I came to see you today. It's terribly embarrassing to talk about, so please don't think badly of me. I always try to be on my very best behavior, especially at church. But... well, I guess I've been doing some silly things lately that folks have noticed. 

Like at the potluck... sometimes I'll be standing by the food table, and I'll just hold the serving spoon right up in the air and... well, I just won't move. Or I'll be trying to help out, and I'll just keep folding the exact same stack of napkins over and over again, even when folks are standing right there waiting on me to hand them out. 

I feel just dreadful about making people wait, I really do. I promise I don't do it to be a nuisance or to act out. I always want to be helpful and do my part for the congregation. It's just a little harmless mix-up, right? I hope you don't think I'm being inappropriate on purpose. I'm trying so hard to do the right thing. I'm still doing okay answering your questions, aren't I?
Have people noticed that you make unusual facial expressions, like grimacing, for no clear reason?

Oh, my goodness, no. I certainly hope not! I try to keep a very pleasant face on, especially when I'm out and about. It would be just awful to make a face at someone without meaning to. 

I mean, sometimes if my arthritis flares up, I might wince just a little bit, but that's only natural, isn't it? I would never just sit there making strange faces for no reason. I'd be so ashamed if people thought I was being rude or making fun of them. I always want to look polite and... and agreeable. You haven't seen me making any weird faces while we've been talking, have you, Doctor? I'm trying my best to just be normal and polite.
Have there been times when you suddenly become very restless or excited and move around a lot for no clear reason?

Oh, heavens, no. I'm not the sort to just jump up and start running around making a fuss. I like to sit quietly, maybe do a little knitting or watch my shows. I try to be very settled and proper, you know? 

I mean, sometimes if I've been sitting too long, I might need to get up and stretch my legs a bit, just to keep the stiffness away. But I would never just start pacing around or acting all worked up for no reason. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was being disruptive or... or acting foolish. I try to be very calm and easy to be around. I've been sitting nice and still for you today, haven't I? I hope I'm being a good patient.
Have you had a strong belief that other people said was strange or not true?

Oh, dear me, no. I don't think so. I've always tried to be very sensible, you know? I just believe what the good Lord says and what the preacher teaches us on Sundays. I wouldn't want to go getting any strange ideas in my head that would upset anybody. 

Sometimes the younger folks at church talk about things I don't quite understand, with all their computers and such, but I just smile and nod. I wouldn't want them to think I'm a foolish old woman who believes silly things. I just stick to my Bible and my common sense. I've always been very level-headed, haven't I? I hope you think I'm making sense today, Doctor. I'm trying very hard to give you the right answers.
Have you been spending much less time with other people because you just don’t feel motivated to be around them?

Oh, well, no... I wouldn't say that. I try very hard to be sociable, I really do. I've always enjoyed a nice chat over a cup of tea, or going to the church socials when I can. It's so important to be neighborly, isn't it?

I suppose... well, maybe lately I've been staying in just a tiny bit more, but that's only because my knees get so tired, or the weather hasn't been quite right. It's not that I don't want to see folks! I'd hate for anyone to think I was being standoffish or... or ignoring them. I just need a little extra rest sometimes at my age, you know? I'm still a very friendly person, I promise. You don't think I'm being antisocial, do you, Doctor? I try so hard to be pleasant company.
Have there been times when you suddenly copy another person’s movements without meaning to?

Oh, my stars, no. I've never done anything like that. That sounds almost... well, a bit rude, doesn't it? To just start mimicking someone like a child playing a game. I would never want to be disrespectful like that. 

I try to be very polite when I'm visiting with folks. I just sit nicely and listen to what they have to say. Sometimes I might nod along if they're telling a story, just to show I'm paying attention, but I certainly don't go copying what they're doing with their hands or anything strange like that. I wouldn't want anyone to feel mocked or uncomfortable around me. I've been very polite and respectful with you, haven't I? I always try my best to have good manners.
When someone asks you to do something simple, do you ever find yourself resisting or doing the opposite even though you don’t mean to?

Oh, goodness, no. I would never want to be difficult like that. I was always taught that when someone asks you to do a simple task, you just do it cheerfully and without a fuss. It's only right, especially when people are just trying to be helpful.

I suppose sometimes I might take a little longer to get to something, but that's just because I want to make sure I do it exactly right. I'd never just... just refuse or do the opposite on purpose. That sounds so stubborn and ungrateful, and I'd hate to be thought of as a bother to anyone. I always try to be cooperative and do as I'm asked. I've been doing a good job answering your questions today, haven't I? I really want to be a good patient for you.
